title: Robert Rubin Warns AI Boom Carries Risks for US Economy, Markets
source_used: Bloomberg text read on Yahoo Finance copy (bloomberg.com returned 403)
key_facts: Former US Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, a former Goldman Sachs co-chairman, spoke at the Greenwich Economic Forum on Tuesday, 6 Oct 2026.
He warned that the AI investment boom could bring major productivity gains and also financial and social risks that markets may not be fully pricing.
He is concerned about 'circularity risk', the overlap of commitments among suppliers, customers and investors, and called the risk of disruption 'not near zero'.
He said AI could hit knowledge workers very hard, with lawyers, accountants and television workers exposed.
He linked the bond market to fiscal worries: 10-year Treasury rates hit their highest level since 2002 that week.
He said AI safety and climate change are 'two massive existential risks' and that the US is still the best place to invest.
quote_evidence: "Some of these very big AI companies have enormous commitments, and then there are a lot of suppliers, and a lot of suppliers have borrowed against those commitments," Rubin said in an interview at the Greenwich Economic Forum Tuesday.
The former Goldman Sachs co-chairman described it as not "near zero."
why_it_matters_hint: A former Treasury chief warns that AI borrowing and commitments could hit markets, workers and fiscal stability.
notes: Event before 7 Oct: stale, score lowered 6 to 5 (-1). Bloomberg original blocked; text is Bloomberg's, read on a Yahoo Finance copy, so Bloomberg is the source.
